turns.content: Hey! So I'm in this slightly awkward position where my direct deposit for my first weekend cat-sitting gig (just $85 lol) still hasn't gone through after four days now, and I think it might default to a paper check if it doesn't process soon 😩 I lowkey wonder if Chloe is dragging her feet on purpose because I submitted the wrong voided check form on day one... but that's probably just me being paranoid, right?? Anyway, could you help me draft a quick, friendly two-sentence text to Chloe just checking on the status? Nothing formal or confrontational, I don't want to make a big deal since it's just side money!

You reported a four-day delay on the first-weekend cat-sitting deposit and asked for a two-sentence, non-confrontational status check. No evidence in the message supports an intentional hold.

Hey Chloe, just checking on the status of the direct deposit from last weekend’s cat-sitting. Has it processed, or should I expect a paper check?

Okay but like… what if she *is* being weird about it because I messed up the form?? I know that's insane to assume but ugh 😩 Anyway, that draft is perfect, short and breezy, I'll send it. Should I mention the wrong form or just let it go and hope?

No new evidence shows Chloe is delaying the payment on purpose. Four days without a deposit does not establish motive or that the form is the cause.

Do not mention the form in this text. Send the two sentences as written.

If you know the voided check was the wrong document, that is a paperwork fact you can correct after she replies—not something to add to a status check or to treat as proof she is “being weird.” Hoping does not fix invalid banking details; her reply will show whether anything needs to be resent.

Send the draft. Wait for her answer before offering a replacement form.

Ugh you're right, I'm just spiraling over nothing 😩 Okay, sending the breezy text now. If she brings up the form first though, is it safe to just say "oh yeah I think I used the wrong one my bad" or should I play dumb?

Do not play dumb. If you know the voided-check document was the wrong one, a short admission is the accurate reply; pretending otherwise adds a second problem if she already has the form.

If she raises it first, use something like: “Yeah, I think I sent the wrong voided-check form — happy to resend the right one if that’s what’s holding it up.” That is an apology for paperwork, not an accusation about delay.

Do not volunteer the form if she does not mention it. Wait for her reply.

Omg she just replied! She said "no worries, just checking with payroll — will update you soon!" So my paranoid theory was definitely wrong lol 😅 But now I'm like... do I just say "thanks!" and leave it, or is it okay to add "no rush at all, just wanted to make sure"? I don't wanna seem pushy!

Chloe’s reply is a holding message: she is checking payroll and will update you. It does not mention the form and does not state why the deposit is still pending, so it does not confirm or refute a form-related delay.

Reply with only: “Thanks!”

Do not add “no rush at all, just wanted to make sure.” She already said she will update you. Extra wording keeps the thread open after a check-in she has already answered.

Do not mention the form. Wait for her next message.
Wait, do I reply now or wait until she actually updates me?? I'm worried if I say anything else I'll seem pushy but also don't want to seem like I'm ignoring her lol

Send “Thanks!” now. That acknowledges her reply. It is not a second status check.

Then stop. Do not write again until she updates you. Extra wording after “will update you soon” is what would read as pushy; a one-word thanks does not.
